title: Correctness and running time of the emitting loop
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines and let $a$ be a state of $B$. Let $I$ be a relation on pairs of Boolean words, let $g,h$ be functions on pairs of Boolean words, and let $s_0$ and $R,T$ be functions as follows: $g(x,s)$ is the next round word, $h(x,s)$ is the output of a round, and $s_0(x)$ is the initial round word. Suppose $F$ computes the function $x\mapsto \operatorname{bits}(R(|x|))$ within time $T$, $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every $x$, and $I(x,s)$ implies $I(x,g(x,s))$. Assume that for each input $x$, the run of $B$ from its initial configuration reaches the seam at state $a$ with word $s_0(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps, without visiting $a$ at any earlier time. Also assume that whenever $I(x,s)$ holds, there is a positive duration at most $T(|x|)$ in which $B$, started at the seam with word $s$, avoids $a$ at all strictly intermediate positive times and ends at the seam with word $g(x,s)$ and output $h(x,s)$. Then the emitting loop machine computes, on every input $x$, the concatenation of the $R(|x|)+1$ round outputs $h(x,g_x^{[i]}(s_0(x)))$ for $0\le i\le R(|x|)$, within time $10(T(|x|)+1)(R(|x|)+2)$, where $g_x(s)=g(x,s)$ and $g_x^{[i]}$ denotes $i$-fold iteration.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean finite machines $B,F$ and anchor state $a$
Initial invariant holds for every input
Invariant is preserved by each round update
Initial run reaches the specified seam within $T(|x|)$ steps without an earlier visit to $a$
Each invariant round has a positive duration at most $T(|x|)$
Each round avoids $a$ at strictly intermediate positive times
Each round ends at the updated seam with its prescribed output
